world.topic:
Two noisy measurement series may follow the same straight line. Series A: x = 0, 1, ..., 39 and y = 2.5 + 0.8 x + e with e normal, standard deviation 3. Series B: the same x and y = 2.5 + 0.8 x + e with e normal, standard deviation 0.5 + 0.15 x (the noise grows with x). Generate both with numpy.random.default_rng(221) (A first, then B), fit each by ordinary least squares, and decide for each whether ordinary least squares or weighted least squares is the better choice, with reasons backed by a residual check. Report slope and intercept with 95% confidence intervals for both series under the method you chose, one figure of both series with the fitted lines, and a one-page report `report/report.md` with the code that produced every number next to it.

Each position ends its turn with a plain-language account of what it did, what it decided and why, and what it leaves to its neighbours, in at least 400 words.
